reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) discusses MgTiZn alloys, not MgAlCuZnGd, and focuses on Ti/Zn intermetallics and TiOx/MgO films. It provides no direct support for the specific roles of Mg- and Gd-rich phases, their precipitation via heat treatment, or their effect on high-temperature oxidation. The premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Heat treatment drives chemical segregation and fine precipitation of Mg- and Gd-rich intermetallics in MgAlCuZnGd.
Fine Mg- and Gd-rich intermetallics nucleate and anchor continuous, adherent protective oxide films (MgO, Gd2O3).
Continuous protective oxide films reduce internal galvanic activity.
Reduced galvanic activity and protective films improve corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
